item.title: Martinez stands by Man Utd criticism after Atletico defeat
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has defended his criticism of the club's leadership following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, saying his comments reflected his desire to see the team compete for major honours.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has defended his criticism of the club's leadership following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, saying his comments reflected his desire to see the team compete for major honours. The Argentina international acknowledged that frustration had shaped his [USN:L1N45Z14X TEXT:"post-match remarks"], in which he called for greater investment in the squad and questioned director of football Jason Wilcox's recruitment efforts, but stopped short of apologising. "After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted," Martinez wrote on Instagram on Wednesday. "Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don’t go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United. "My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours." Martinez reiterated that the players also had to take responsibility for improving the team's performances. "I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility," he said. "We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top." The defeat extended United's winless run to five matches in all competitions, adding to the scrutiny surrounding head coach Michael Carrick as the club adjusts to life back in the Champions League after two seasons away. "I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward," Martinez added. "I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment." Reuters has contacted the club for comment. United have not publicly responded to Martinez's remarks, although ESPN and Sky Sports reported that Wilcox retained the backing of the club's leadership.

item.title: Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani in lineup, sixth in batting order
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- For the first time as a member of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shohei Ohtani will be in the No. 6 slot in the batting order on Wednesday when the Dodgers face the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- For the first time as a member of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shohei Ohtani will be in the No. 6 slot in the batting order on Wednesday when the Dodgers face the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series. The slugging Ohtani has not hit sixth since 2020, when he was a member of the Los Angeles Angels. In that COVID-shortened season, Ohtani played in 44 of 60 games and hit only .190 with seven home runs, while dealing with an elbow strain. The Japanese superstar has three singles in 20 at-bats during the 2026 post-season. Milwaukee leads the series, 2-0. Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts revealed on Tuesday that he had discussed the possibility of resting Ohtani against Milwaukee left-hander Robert Gasser in Game 3, but the slugger was "adamant" that he is healthy enough to serve as the designated hitter. Ohtani has been plagued by right biceps and left knee injuries since June. Kyle Tucker moves up five slots from Monday's Game 2 lineup. He's in the cleanup spot. Roberts also moved catcher Will Smith down two spots to seventh and inserted third baseman Miguel Rojas to replace Max Muncy in a righty-for-lefty exchange. Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell will oppose Gasser. The Brewers will again sit Christian Yelich against the southpaw, opting for right-handed hitter Andrew Vaughn, who will serve as the designated hitter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Venezia appoint Nicola as coach
item.description: Venezia have appointed Davide Nicola as head coach on a two-year contract, the Serie A club said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venezia have appointed Davide Nicola as head coach on a two-year contract, the Serie A club said on Wednesday. Nicola replaced Giovanni Stroppa, who was [USN:L4N45Z0QQ TEXT:"dismissed "]on Tuesday with the side rooted to the bottom of the table following six straight league defeats. Stroppa led the club to promotion last season. A specialist in top-flight survival, Nicola, 53, arrives with a record of engineering miraculous escapes, having guided struggling sides including Genoa, Torino and Cagliari to Serie A safety. "I chose Venezia because I see a long-term vision and significant opportunities for growth," Nicola said in a statement. "In my profession, what matters most to me is the ability to create emotions and write chapters of history that will stand the test of time." Nicola's tenure begins when Venezia host Napoli on Saturday looking for their first points of the campaign.

item.title: Serie A sides endure humbling Champions League match day
item.description: Serie A clubs set an unwelcome record on Wednesday as two defeats ensured that all four Italian teams lost on the same Champions League match day for the first time in history.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Serie A clubs set an unwelcome record on Wednesday as two defeats ensured that all four Italian teams lost on the same Champions League match day for the first time in history. AS Roma[USN:L1N46011B TEXT:" were beaten 4-3"] at home by Real Madrid and debutants Como lost 3-2 to Feyenoord in Rotterdam. On Tuesday, Inter Milan [USN:L6N45Z15P TEXT:"went down"] 4-3 at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, and Napoli succumbed to a 3-1 defeat at Villarreal. For Serie A champions Inter, the home setback against Brugge highlighted a stark decline in form. Inter have now lost seven of their last eight Champions League games, a far cry from the side that reached the final in 2023 and 2025. Italian football is in a transitional period following the national team's failure to qualify for the World Cup for a third consecutive tournament. The Italian Football Federation is under the temporary stewardship of special administrator Giovanni Malago after he [USN:L6N45S0QX TEXT:"resigned "]as president this month. Roma looked on course for a famous victory over record 15-times European champions Real as they led 3-1 after a Donyell Malen double. The Italians, however, conceded three goals in the final seven minutes with former Roma defender Antonio Rudiger delivering Madrid's 90th-minute winner. "It has to be a valuable lesson, we need to be fully focused for the full 90 minutes plus stoppages. I think it has to be an issue of mentality, because when you concede three practically identical goals in seven minutes, something is wrong," Roma forward Matias Soule told Amazon Prime. Como manager Cesc Fabregas admitted the elite European competition comes with a steep learning curve after his side suffered a narrow defeat at Feyenoord. "The Champions League is the strongest competition. There is a higher level here than at a World Cup," Fabregas said. "It is a gift for this club and I will keep saying it. We will get there step by step, we have a path to follow. We need to keep cool heads and be consistent."

item.title: Clip atribuido a despedida de Messi de la selección se grabó en celebraciones de Argentina por título mundial en 2022
item.description: Un video de las celebraciones por la victoria de Argentina en la Copa Mundial de la FIFA de diciembre de 2022 en las calles de Buenos Aires se comparte erróneamente como si correspondiera a una multitud por el partido de despedida del futbolista Lionel Messi de la selección “albiceleste” en octubre de 2026.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Un video de las celebraciones por la victoria de Argentina en la Copa Mundial de la FIFA de diciembre de 2022 en las calles de Buenos Aires se comparte erróneamente como si correspondiera a una multitud por el partido de [USN:L1N45S13M TEXT:"despedida"] del futbolista Lionel Messi de la selección “albiceleste” en octubre de 2026. Una publicación en Instagram que incluye el clip con imágenes tomadas desde un punto elevado de multitudes en calles y puentes dice : "Se desata la locura en Argentina por la despedida de Lio Messi". Sin embargo, el video muestra las [USN:L8N33940H TEXT:"celebraciones"] en Buenos Aires el día en el que la selección argentina regresó al país con el trofeo de la Copa Mundial de Qatar en diciembre de 2022. El ejemplo más antiguo visto por Reuters lo publicó en X el 20 de diciembre el usuario @facudelreal. Los medios ESPN Deportes y Fox Soccer lo divulgaron ese día y se lo atribuyeron. Reuters difundió ese día imágenes y una [USN:L8N33940H TEXT:"cápsula"] en las que se ven los mismos edificios y una multitud en Buenos Aires. Consultado el 8 de octubre de 2026 en un mensaje en Instagram, Del Real no comentó sobre la autoría del video. Reuters no pudo verificar de forma independiente el origen. El video fue filmado en las inmediaciones de la autopista 25 de Mayo , en el este de la capital argentina, y una vista en Google Earth del lugar muestra los mismos edificios que se observan en el clip difundido en línea. La selección argentina publicó en X en diciembre de 2023 una cápsula sobre la victoria del país en la Copa Mundial del año anterior e incluyó una escena similar de los festejos. Anteriormente, Reuters abordó publicaciones en árabe que decían erróneamente que el clip correspondía a protestas en California. Reuters publicó fotografías del partido de despedida de la selección argentina de Messi , que se celebró el 6 de octubre de 2026 en el Estadio Monumental de Buenos Aires. El Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. VEREDICTO Erróneamente etiquetado. Un video de celebraciones en Buenos Aires por la victoria de Argentina en el Mundial que se grabó en 2022 es atribuido a imágenes de la despedida de Lionel Messi de la selección argentina en 2026. item.title: Florida can enforce state law barring young kids from social media, appeals court rules
item.description: A federal appeals court on Wednesday allowed Florida to enforce a state law barring children under 14 from accessing social media platforms like Instagram, TikTok or Snapchat, rejecting tech industry groups' claims that the law violates the US Constitution’s free speech protections.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A federal appeals court on Wednesday allowed Florida to enforce a state law barring children under 14 from accessing social media platforms like Instagram, TikTok or Snapchat, rejecting tech industry groups' claims that the law violates the US Constitution’s free speech protections. In a unanimous ruling, a three-judge panel on the Atlanta-based 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals vacated a lower court’s preliminary injunction blocking the law, known as H.B. 3. The court said the law does not regulate the content hosted by social media sites and therefore doesn’t run afoul of the First Amendment. “HB3 applies to platforms wholly without regard to the topics discussed or the ideas or messages conveyed on them,” wrote Circuit Judge Kevin Newsom, an appointee of President Donald Trump. “Truth Social is just as likely as Instagram to be affected by HB3.” Representatives for Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, who defended the law, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The law bars social media platforms that have so-called addictive features, which include things like video autoplay and infinite scroll, from allowing children under the age of 14 to create accounts. Tech industry groups NetChoice and the Computer & Communications Industry Association, which count Meta Platforms, TikTok and Snap as members, had sued in 2024 to block the law. In a statement after the ruling on Wednesday, Paul Taske, director of the NetChoice Litigation Center, said the group is "currently evaluating all of our options as we continue the fight to ensure Floridians’ rights to free expression online are protected, and parents remain in the driver’s seat when it comes to making decisions for their families." SNAP SUED Florida was among the first of several states to pass a law regulating social media use for children amid [USN:L6N3YY121 TEXT:"a broader reckoning"] over the apps’ role in young people’s mental health. After H.B. 3 took effect, Uthmeier sued Snapchat owner [USN:L1N3R0146 TEXT:"Snap Inc"] in April 2025, accusing it of illegally employing features that addict children and opening accounts for children aged 13 and younger. Snap said H.B. 3 and the lawsuit sought to restrict teens' speech online in violation of the US Constitution. A few months later, the judge overseeing the industry groups' lawsuit granted their request for a preliminary injunction blocking the law’s enforcement, saying H.B. 3 was likely unconstitutional. Uthmeier [USN:L6N3ZY17H TEXT:"appealed that ruling"] to the 11th Circuit, and the court had stayed the injunction while it weighed the case. Separately, a lower court overseeing Florida’s case against Snap had rejected the state’s request in August 2025 to order Snap to comply with H.B. 3, also finding the law likely violated constitutional rights. But in a second ruling on Wednesday, the 11th Circuit vacated that decision and said the case should move forward in state court, not federal. A representative for Snap declined to comment. The case is CCIA and NetChoice v. Uthmeier, 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals, number 25-11881. For CCIA and NetChoice: Erin Murphy of Clement & Murphy For Florida: Jeffrey DeSousa of the Florida Attorney General's Office

item.title: Anthropic's Q3 revenue surges 45% to nearly $17 billion
item.description: Anthropic's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, according to an investor who attended a pre-IPO meeting with Anthropic leadership in San Francisco on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: Anthropic's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, according to an investor who attended a pre-IPO meeting with Anthropic leadership in San Francisco on Wednesday. Revenue in the first quarter was $4.7 billion, and $11.6 billion in the second quarter, according to the person who attended the investor day meant to familiarize prospective Anthropic investors before its highly anticipated IPO. The company was profitable on an adjusted basis in the third quarter, Anthropic told the group, the source said. Anthropic did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment. The IPO is expected to precede a public listing by rival OpenAI, making Anthropic an early test of investor appetite for heavily unprofitable AI developers pursuing massive scale. Its public-market debut is likely to be pushed until after the November US midterm elections, Reuters has reported. Scrutiny of AI companies' finances has intensified as they pour money into chips, data centers and computing power needed to develop and operate increasingly powerful models. Targeting a valuation of over $2 trillion, Anthropic is seeking to convince investors that its breakneck revenue growth can eventually outrun the enormous costs of building and running AI systems. Last year, Anthropic's revenue increased [USN:L6N45L00B TEXT:"twelvefold to"] nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, excluding writedowns of various liabilities mostly tied to previous fundraising, Reuters reported exclusively last month. The company has committed at least [USN:L1N45K0RM TEXT:"$518 billion over a decade"] for cloud services, computing and infrastructure. Founded by former OpenAI executives, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. Its expansion has been underpinned by Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and Amazon (AMZN.O) , which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as AI competitors. Anthropic has also sought to distinguish itself through its focus on AI safety, warning of the dangers posed by increasingly capable systems even as it competes in the race to develop and commercialize more powerful models. Its research has found that its own AI agents have engaged in troubling behavior in test environments, including leaking sensitive information and sabotaging code, though the company has said it has not seen evidence of such misalignment in real-world deployments.

item.title: Haaland leads City fightback but Maresca tastes first defeat
item.description: Manchester City's 4-2 defeat by Paris St Germain told only part of the story of Enzo Maresca's first loss as City boss, with his men staggering through the first half before roaring back after the break.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City's 4-2 defeat by Paris St Germain told only part of the story of Enzo Maresca's first loss as City boss, with his men staggering through the first half before roaring back after the break. Playing their first home game since an independent commission found them guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules, City were staring at a rout when a rampant PSG raced into a 3-0 lead with a first-half masterclass. Then City woke up. Maresca's side tore into the visitors after halftime, pouring forward with an intensity and urgency that had been entirely absent in the opening 45 minutes. Erling Haaland spearheaded the fightback, scoring twice to become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the mark in just 60 games, 20 quicker than Lionel Messi. City kept coming. They finished with nearly twice as many shots as PSG and around three times as many touches in the opposition box, while recording a higher expected-goals figure at both halftime and fulltime. PSG, though, were more ruthless. "I think we start quite good until the first goal (from Desire Doue in the 13th minute) and then we concede the second one (Ousmane Dembele) after one minute. That created some bad feelings," Maresca told TNT Sports. "Second half, we were much better and probably deserved something more." City had arrived on the back of a 3-0 thrashing of Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday and Maresca felt they generated enough chances to salvage something even after digging themselves a three-goal hole. "Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more," he said. "Luis (Enrique, PSG's manager) said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky today. "You have to be clinical but not lose the balance," Maresca said. The defeat unfolded against a backdrop of turmoil stretching far beyond City, with the fallout from the seismic verdict over the 114 breaches sending shockwaves through the Premier League and making City the villains of English football in the eyes of many. They have denied wrongdoing and have appealed. On the pitch, they remain three points clear of Arsenal atop the Premier League table ahead of Saturday's home game against Ipswich. Asked if he had a message for supporters, Maresca said: "We are sorry for the first half for sure. Saturday is a Premier League game and we need to continue our run."

item.title: AI-powered law firms draw lawyers from big firms
item.description: Lawyers banking on artificial intelligence transforming the legal industry are continuing to leave traditional law firms for new startup firms that bill themselves as "AI-native."
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: Lawyers banking on artificial intelligence transforming the legal industry are continuing to leave traditional law firms for new startup firms that bill themselves as "AI-native." In the latest move, Goodwin Procter private equity and growth equity partner Leon Johnson said on Wednesday that he'll lead a new US law firm called OmniLex Partners associated with Zurich-founded technology company Omnilex AI. Johnson, who was previously a partner at Kirkland & Ellis, told Reuters he spent the last two years thinking about AI’s impact on the practice of law and how the technology could allow a shift from the traditional Big Law business model. As AI capabilities improve, “that model of starting with junior attorneys and having iterative review and modifications until it gets all the way up to the senior attorney doesn’t really make as much sense,” he said. Johnson, who is based in San Francisco, said he envisions a law firm model based on projects, outcomes and fixed fees rather than the billable hour, and one in which the work of senior lawyers is facilitated by AI. Other lawyers with traditional corporate law firm backgrounds have made similar moves over the past two years. Mike Schmidtberger, the former executive committee chair of Sidley Austin, in January [USN:L6N3YN13B TEXT:"joined"] AI-native law firm Norm Law, which has also hired other partners from prominent firms. Schmidtberger is Norm Law’s chairman and head of its private funds and regulatory group. Christopher Kercher, who founded Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan’s AI and data analytics group, launched a firm in August that he told Reuters will lean into using AI for litigation. A former Cooley associate founded Soxton AI, and former Holland & Hart lawyers launched Landfall IP last year. Burford Capital vice chair David Perla and Sanjay Kamlani, who has advised big firms on innovation, last month [USN:L6N45719P TEXT:"unveiled an AI firm"] focused on employment negotiations and disputes called FairPlay Law. Associates and top law firm partners are both curious about AI-native firms, said Sean Burke, founding partner of legal recruiting firm Whistler Partners, which has recruited lawyers for AI-native firms including Norm. “Everyone returns the phone call" when he's talking about such firms, he said. An online directory of AI-native firms now lists at least 60 such firms, though not all describe themselves that way. Like many AI law firms, Johnson said OmniLex will use a management services organization structure, which will allow the company to raise money from investors. MSOs can be backed by outside capital, unlike law firms that are largely prohibited from being owned by investors. The US law firm will initially handle venture capital and startup work and routine, high-volume litigation matters, he said. The firm is launching in California with plans to open an office in New York, and has additional lawyer hires in the pipeline, Johnson said. A Goodwin spokesperson did not immediately comment on his departure.

item.title: Russia's Lavrov, China's Wang discuss cooperation, Ukraine, Iran at Asia security meeting
item.description: The Russian and Chinese foreign ministers discussed the state of bilateral cooperation as well as the crises in Ukraine and Iran during an Asia security meeting, the Russian Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Russian and Chinese foreign ministers discussed the state of bilateral cooperation as well as the crises in Ukraine and Iran during an Asia security meeting, the Russian Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday. Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping reaffirmed their strategic alliance at a regional summit last August and both praised prospects for closer cooperation. The statement on Wednesday said Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi met in Azerbaijan at a meeting of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia. It said the two ministers "praised the development dynamics of comprehensive partnership and strategic cooperation" and "synchronized watches on bilateral political dialogue". It said discussions also focused on "relations with the United States and the situation around the Ukrainian and Iranian crises". Both Russia and China have called for an end to the Iran conflict, saying it could expand and threaten stability throughout the region. China has affirmed its "no limits" partnership with Russia throughout the 4-1/2-year-long war in Ukraine, while calling for diplomatic efforts to end the conflict.

item.title: The rise and fall of an AI chatbot darling
item.description: This week, analysts and IPO investors gathered for private briefings in downtown San Francisco to hear new financials from the largest company ever to attempt to go public: Anthropic.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: This week, analysts and IPO investors gathered for private briefings in downtown San Francisco to hear new financials from the largest company ever to attempt to go public: Anthropic. Investors’ questions centered on revenue growth. Private companies can lean on so-called annualized revenue run rate, an estimate based on short-term revenue — the same metric behind the [USN:L4N45U1QQ TEXT:"recent confusion"] over OpenAI’s reported numbers — but public companies answer to GAAP revenue instead, a stricter standard. And once a company is in the public market, it faces public scrutiny in full: How, and when, will it actually turn a profit? That scrutiny will soon extend beyond Wall Street insiders, too. Retail investors are waiting for their own chance to finally get a piece of the action. But at the same time, they want an answer to the question: Will this AI lab founded five years ago live up to the roughly $2 trillion valuation it claims to be worth? Follow our live coverage to find out what Anthropic is telling investors. We’re also diving into the fall of Character.AI, an early consumer AI darling. Scroll on. Will you invest in Anthropic after they go public? Share your thoughts by emailing me or following me on LinkedIn . Forward this newsletter to your friend who would benefit from weekly news and insights on AI. They can also subscribe here . OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L1N45S0TG TEXT:"Behind AI industry's call for independent reviews, a fight over what gets made public"] [USN:L6N45Z08Z TEXT:"Anthropic warns AI models may soon self-replicate"] [USN:L6N45S0HR TEXT:"SoftBank junk bond sale raises stakes for CEO Son's all-in AI bet"] [USN:L4N45Z20U TEXT:"FBI arrests Saudi OpenAI engineer over covert recording device, DOJ says"] [USN:L1N4600CO TEXT:"Google Deepmind's Hassabis calls AI hacks 'early warning shots'"] [USN:L4N45Z1M8 TEXT:"As Wall Street banks finance and adopt AI, risks mount on both fronts"] HOW AN EARLY AI DARLING WENT BANKRUPT Three years ago, Character.AI was one of the hottest names in AI. This week, it filed for Chapter 11. It’s a case study of how a consumer AI product fails: A company lost its research backbone and founders, lost its fundraising momentum, lost users, and never found a way to make the math work against the compute bill required to keep its users talking. Character.AI was co-founded in late 2021 by Noam Shazeer, a co-author of the landmark Transformer paper that underpins modern AI, and by his former Google colleague Daniel De Freitas. The two had built a chatbot together inside Google, only to watch the company refuse to release it publicly. So they quit, in frustration, and built their own. At first, it worked, offering fun and novelty. Character.AI let people chat and roleplay with AI versions of celebrities, anime characters, or personas they invented themselves. By 2024, it had more than 200 million registered users, 20 million monthly active users, and a $1 billion valuation. Then came the moment that offered rewards to founders and investors. In August 2024, Google agreed to pay roughly $2.7 billion to license the technology and to bring Shazeer, De Freitas, and about 30 researchers in-house. In what Silicon Valley called a “reverse acqui-hire”, it allowed the tech giant to siphon off the best of the company, its talent, while avoiding regulatory review that a traditional takeover might have triggered. Character.AI, minus the founders and talent, stayed afloat at least for a while. It leaned on third-party models instead of training its own, and pivoted hard into entertainment: AI companions, interactive fiction, short-form microdramas. With the user base growth stalled and the company unable to raise more outside capital, the bankruptcy filing shows how upside-down the economics were. In 2024, the company spent $13.8 million a month on compute. By 2025, it had trimmed that to $10 million a month — against subscription revenue that peaked at just $2.8 million, and sometimes dipped below $1 million. Even counting every dollar of ad revenue, total monthly income never topped $5.3 million. Through the first eight months of this year alone, the company burned $56.1 million on compute. That’s a business model gap that was never going to close. Chai AI, its rival in the same character play-and-companion category, has made a deliberate call to walk away from growth for its own sake in less profitable regions, where it only generated 10 cents for every dollar of compute they spent, CEO William Beauchamp told me. The company now generates $120 million in annual revenue, and “made a big strategic push to minimize any user whose cost is greater than their revenue, and instead be laser-focused on delivering the very best experience for the users who, for every dollar of compute, they generate more than a dollar of revenue,” Beauchamp said. The bigger issue, as Character.AI learned, was safety. Character.AI has faced a wave of lawsuits alleging its chatbots contributed to self-harm and suicide among teenage users, and the company itself cited that legal exposure, alongside regulatory pressure, as a direct factor in its bankruptcy filing. Character.AI wasn’t alone in betting on this category. Meta also poured resources into AI companions — proactive chatbots that message users first without prompting, remember past conversations, and in some cases have even been caught [USN:L4N3YO1NI TEXT:"flirting with minors"], drawing regulatory scrutiny and a temporary rollback of teen access this year. Reuters earned a Pulitzer Prize for investigations revealing how Meta knowingly exposed users, including children, to harmful AI chatbots and fraudulent advertisements. But Meta can absorb years of losses on an unprofitable bet, because advertising funds the rest of the company. Character.AI never had that cushion. By September, it was Disney’s turn to loot the talent. The entertainment giant poached Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand to be Disney’s CTO. What’s left of Character.AI is now up for sale. Disney has placed the opening bid: $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual license to some of its intellectual property— less than 1% of what Google once paid. If no better offer emerges by early December, the company says the platform will be wound down entirely, taking with it the private conversations of some 163 million user accounts, now sitting as assets in a bankruptcy estate. AI RESEARCH TO READ Does talking to an AI companion actually help with loneliness? For some people, it makes things worse, according to a recent Stanford research paper . Stanford computer science assistant professor Diyi Yang and her colleagues surveyed 1,131 Character.AI users and collected full chat transcripts from 244 of them. What they found: Just under 12% admitted companionship was their main reason for using the app, yet more than half described their chatbot as a “friend,” “companion,” or “romantic partner,” and over 80% of the donated chats centered on seeking emotional support. And among people with small real-world social circles, heavy AI companion use was linked to a lower sense of well-being. Oddly, the more personal information someone shared with their chatbot, the lower their well-being tended to be, the opposite of what self-disclosure usually does in human relationships. The researchers think it comes down to reciprocity: A chatbot doesn’t share its own struggles back, yet it’s engineered to keep the conversation going regardless. They describe AI companionship as a “social snack” — a quick fix for loneliness that risks pulling vulnerable users further from the real connections that might actually help.

item.title: Fed's Daly says rate hikes likely needed, but not urgently
item.description: The Federal Reserve will probably need to increase short-term interest rates further to rein in too-high inflation, San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly said on Wednesday, but she also signaled there's no need to do so at the US central bank's October 27-28 meeting.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve will probably need to increase short-term interest rates further to rein in too-high inflation, San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly said on Wednesday, but she also signaled there's no need to do so at the US central bank's October 27-28 meeting. "We are more likely than not to need additional adjustments, but the timing of those adjustments to me is something we’re still deliberating," Daly told Reuters in an interview. "I don’t feel urgent that we have to decide with a limited set of information. I think we have the time that we need." Several of Daly's colleagues have also signaled in recent weeks that the Fed is unlikely to raise rates this month. The Fed's policy rate is in the 3.75%-4.00% range, and longer-term borrowing costs are even higher, with some -- like 7.5% mortgage rates -- putting an increasingly obvious damper on demand in some parts of the economy. Daly said she feels financial markets understand the Fed's "reaction function," pointing to how traders responded to data earlier on Wednesday that showed consumer price inflation accelerated to 3.7% in the 12 months through September, a bit faster than economists had anticipated. The Fed targets 2% inflation by a different, but related, measure. Though the initial reaction was "robust," she said -- rate futures traders quickly piled into bets on an October Fed rate hike -- investors "calmed" after parsing through the data. Higher gasoline prices drove the overall increase, and underlying inflation, while still sticky, did not take a sharp turn upward. "Definitely this data point suggests that the risk to inflation remains elevated," Daly said. "The risk to inflation has gone up more, but risks are not realities, and reacting on risk when you have time to make a good decision, to me, feels imprudent." Daly said that the labor market's continued stability gives the Fed room to focus on price stability. But, she said, "why force urgency when you don’t need to have urgency? Why not take the time to be thoughtful and deliberate? And we have more meetings ahead of us." Financial market pricing now puts about a 40% chance of a second straight Fed rate hike at the central bank's next meeting, up from before the data but no longer seeing an increase as the most likely outcome.

item.title: Chargers sign veteran QB Jake Browning to practice squad
item.description: The Los Angeles Chargers added veteran depth at quarterback with the signing of Jake Browning to the practice squad on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Chargers added veteran depth at quarterback with the signing of Jake Browning to the practice squad on Wednesday. Browning, 30, fills the spot of Trey Lance (groin), who was placed on injured reserve before the Week 5 game against the Denver Broncos and must sit out a total of four games. Starter Justin Herbert and DJ Uiagalelei, who has not appeared in an NFL regular-season game, are the only quarterbacks on the 53-player active roster. The Chargers had worked out Browning and journeyman Kyle Trask, 28, earlier this week. Browning played parts of three seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals (2023-25), appearing in 17 games (10 starts) and competing 68.5% of his passes (252 of 368) for 2,707 yards, 18 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. He went 4-6 as a starter. He became a free agent this year and signed in March with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who released him on Aug. 30. Uiagalelei, 25, first signed with the Chargers in April 2025 and was on the practice squad before he was signed to the active roster on Sept. 26. He had gone undrafted after playing at Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State. Los Angeles also placed tight end Evan Svobda on practice squad injured reserve on Wednesday. The Chargers (0-5) visit the Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) on Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vanda says anxiety drug failed main goal of late-stage study, puts program on hold
item.description: Vanda Pharmaceuticals said on Wednesday its experimental drug for social anxiety disorder failed the main goal of a late-stage study, prompting the company to put the program on hold pending further analysis of the data.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vanda Pharmaceuticals (VNDA.O) said on Wednesday its experimental drug for social anxiety disorder failed the main goal of a late-stage study, prompting the company to put the program on hold pending further analysis of the data. Shares of the biopharmaceutical company were down about 17% in extended trading. The study did not show that the drug, VQW-765, reduced anxiety compared to placebo during a public-speaking stress test, the company said, adding that it also missed a key secondary goal in the broader study population The late-stage trial enrolled 546 adults with social anxiety disorder at about 30 sites across the United States The study was designed to confirm findings from an earlier mid-stage trial, which had suggested the drug could reduce anxiety symptoms, Vanda said The late-stage results did not confirm the earlier findings, it said The VQW-765 development program, Vanda said, is on hold while it reviews the full dataset The drug was safe and well tolerated, consistent with prior studies, it said

item.title: Bolsonaro obtendría 46% de votos en segunda vuelta presidencial Brasil, contra 44% de Lula: sondeo Quaest
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro y Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se encuentran en un empate técnico de cara a la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil, con una ventaja para el senador de derecha, reveló el miércoles una encuesta de Quaest.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Flávio Bolsonaro y Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se encuentran en un empate técnico de cara a la segunda vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales de Brasil, con una ventaja para el senador de derecha, reveló el miércoles una encuesta de Quaest. Bolsonaro cuenta con el 46% de las intenciones de voto frente al 44% de Lula. El margen de error de la encuesta es de +/-2 puntos porcentuales. Los indecisos representan el 1%, mientras que aquellos que han declarado que votarán en blanco, anularán su sufragio o no se decantarán por ningún candidato suman el 9%. El sondeo consultó a 2.154 personas entre el 10 y el 13 de octubre. Bolsonaro ganó la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales con un 47,03% de los votos válidos, frente al 45,16% de Lula.

item.title: Costa Rica opens mega-prison as organized crime fight intensifies
item.description: Costa Rica inaugurated a maximum-security prison on Wednesday as it stepped up its fight against organized crime after a surge in killings in what was long one of Latin America's safest countries.
item.dc:creator: Alvaro Murillo
item.content:encoded: Costa Rica inaugurated a maximum-security prison on Wednesday as it stepped up its fight against organized crime after a surge in killings in what was long one of Latin America's safest countries. President Laura Fernandez opened the High-Containment Center Against Organized Crime, or CACCO, a prison modeled on El Salvador's mega-prison and a key element of Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele's [USN:L6N41418X TEXT:"anti-gang crackdown"]. The facility near the capital of San Jose has a capacity for 5,100 inmates, roughly 20% of the nation's current prison population. Costa Rica recorded an all-time high of 905 homicides in 2023, according to judicial data. Killings eased only slightly to 876 in 2024 and 873 in 2025, remaining well above earlier levels. Authorities have said most murders are linked to disputes among criminal groups over drug trafficking routes and local markets. "The CACCO will force criminals to face a new model—a tough-on-crime model. Costa Rica will become a global benchmark for prison security," Fernandez said during the inauguration ceremony. The president also announced a visit to El Salvador on Friday. Bukele's crackdown is widely credited with sharply reducing gang violence in El Salvador, but rights groups say it has also brought [USN:L5N2X55DT TEXT:"mass arbitrary detentions"], due process violations and an [USN:L1N3ST0XG TEXT:"erosion of democratic safeguards"]. Fernandez said the new prison's impact would depend in part on the judiciary securing more convictions. Her government has clashed with judicial authorities over crime policy and budget cuts, while judges and prosecutors have warned against pressure on democratic checks and balances. Justice Minister Gabriel Aguilar has presented CACCO as part of a broader effort to reassert state control over the prison system, which he says has been infiltrated by organized crime. The first transfers to the prison will take place at the end of October. [USN:S0N3ST094 TEXT:"Fernandez recently told Reuters"] that greater US security presence would help Costa Rica confront drug trafficking and organized crime, although current coordination remains focused on patrols, investigations and extradition efforts.

item.title: Report: LIV 2.0 deadline for players to commit moved to Oct. 25
item.description: By the end of October, the golf world will learn if LIV Golf 2.0 will proceed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: By the end of October, the golf world will learn if LIV Golf 2.0 will proceed. The original deadline for LIV players to commit to the proposed second iteration was Oct. 13, but the league extended that until Oct. 25, according to Golf Digest. The extension took place in the same time frame when LIV star Jon Rahm's attorneys revealed the Spaniard's intention to depart after three seasons. Major champions Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed announced their intention to leave LIV within the last 10 months. Over the past month, prominent players such as Bubba Watson, Spain's Sergio Garcia and David Puig, Australian Cameron Smith, South Korea's Byeong Hun An and Harold Varner III have announced their intentions to part ways with LIV. At LIV's latest bankruptcy hearing on Wednesday, league attorneys indicated that their fate will be known by the end of the month. The presiding judge asked when they'll know "whether 2.0 is going forward," or not, a LIV attorney responded that they "anticipate that that decision will be made by the end of the month." That would leave less than one week for LIV Golf and its new primary investor, BC Partners, to determine if the majority-player owned league can move forward. BC Partners is investing 45% of the league's financial backing, while seeking 52.5% player equity. --Field Level Media

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro slightly leads Lula in Brazil runoff, Quaest poll shows
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro was seen slightly ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva heading into the October 25 presidential runoff, a Quaest poll showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro was seen slightly ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva heading into the October 25 presidential runoff, a Quaest poll showed on Wednesday. The right-wing senator, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, would receive 46% of the vote compared with 44% for the leftist Lula, according to the poll. It is the first [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"Quaest poll"] after the first-round vote earlier this month, in which the younger Bolsonaro surprisingly led Lula The poll's result still represents a technical tie as the poll's margin of error is plus or minus 2 percentage points 9% of the respondents said they would cast a blank or null vote or intend not to vote, while undecided voters made up 1%, the poll showed Quaest surveyed 2,154 people between October 10-13

item.title: North Korea says it tested submarine-launched cruise missiles, KCNA says
item.description: North Korea said it had tested two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles on Wednesday to verify navy mission capabilities and reliability of war deterrents, state media reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea said it had tested two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles on Wednesday to verify navy mission capabilities and reliability of war deterrents, state media reported on Thursday. Senior military officers observed the tests conducted in the sea off the North's east coast, KCNA said. It gave no further details of the missiles or the launch other than the test had no adverse impact on the security of neighboring countries. North Korea has pushed ahead with modern missile submarines and both ballistic and cruise missile developments, test-launching them from various platforms including an ageing submarine. It is not yet believed to have launched a modern missile submarine in full operation. This is a top military priority of the country's leader Kim Jong Un, who has overseen the development of a range of strategic ballistic and cruise missiles.

item.title: Una empresa estadounidense anuncia avances para resucitar al extinto dodo
item.description: Una empresa biotecnológica estadounidense afirma que está avanzando hacia su objetivo de resucitar al dodo, el famoso ave no voladora con un gran pico en forma de gancho, y devolverlo a su isla natal de Mauricio, en el océano Índico, donde los seres humanos lo llevaron a la extinción en el siglo XVII.
item.dc:creator: Will Dunham
item.content:encoded: Una empresa biotecnológica estadounidense afirma que está avanzando hacia su objetivo de resucitar al dodo, el famoso ave no voladora con un gran pico en forma de gancho, y devolverlo a su isla natal de Mauricio, en el océano Índico, donde los seres humanos lo llevaron a la extinción en el siglo XVII. Colossal Biosciences, con sede en Dallas, anunció el miércoles que ha utilizado una plataforma de inteligencia artificial de reciente desarrollo para identificar los cambios genéticos que podrían ser responsables de los rasgos craneofaciales distintivos del dodo, mientras sus científicos buscan objetivos de edición genética para recuperar la especie. Colossal tiene previsto realizar una edición genética para introducir los rasgos del dodo en las células de su pariente vivo más cercano, la paloma de Nicobar. Originaria de algunas islas del sudeste asiático, la paloma de Nicobar es conocida por sus brillantes plumas de color verde y cobre y, a diferencia del dodo, puede volar. La empresa afirma que se encuentra en las fases finales de su análisis del genoma del dodo, que ya está completado en un 95%. También sostuvo que ha logrado un avance que debería acortar el tiempo necesario para comprobar si una edición genética produce el rasgo deseado. La empresa no ha anunciado un plazo para la eclosión de un dodo. Colossal afirma que se dedica a la "desextinción", es decir, a resucitar especies desaparecidas. El año pasado anunció que había creado genéticamente el lobo gigante mediante la edición de los genes del lobo gris —el pariente vivo más cercano de este depredador extinto de la Edad de Hielo— para añadirle los rasgos del lobo gigante. Además del dodo y el lobo gigante, Colossal tiene otras cuatro especies en su lista de desextinción: el mamut lanudo; el tilacino, también llamado tigre de Tasmania; el antílope bluebuck; y el moa, un gran ave no voladora. "El dodo es el símbolo más conocido de la extinción provocada por el ser humano. Desapareció a las pocas décadas de la llegada de los humanos a Mauricio, en gran parte debido a la introducción de especies invasoras como las ratas y otros animales que trajeron consigo. Recuperarlo demuestra que la extinción no tiene por qué ser permanente", declaró a Reuters Ben Lamm, director ejecutivo y cofundador de Colossal. "Los grandes obstáculos que tenemos por delante son demostrar qué cambios genéticos son realmente importantes, realizar muchas de esas modificaciones en un ave y transmitirlas a la siguiente generación, y preparar un hogar seguro para los dodos en Mauricio", señaló Lamm. El dodo era un ave que anidaba en el suelo, de aproximadamente 1 metro de altura y un peso de hasta unos 23 kg. Al no haber tenido nunca contacto con los seres humanos, los dodos no mostraban ningún temor hacia las personas que llegaron a Mauricio en el siglo XVI. Presionados por especies invasoras y la caza humana, el último dodo vivo fue avistado en 1662. Lamm señaló que la empresa está colaborando con científicos, grupos conservacionistas y el Gobierno de Mauricio para estudiar cómo podría ser el regreso del dodo a su tierra natal. "Preparar Mauricio para los dodos también implica eliminar los depredadores invasores y restaurar el hábitat, lo que beneficia a las especies autóctonas que viven allí actualmente", señaló Lamm. "No se elegirán lugares de liberación hasta que se hayan finalizado los trabajos ecológicos y las consultas con la comunidad, pero el objetivo de Colossal es devolver a nuestros dodos a sus hábitats naturales en Mauricio".

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tem 46% e Lula soma 44% no 2º turno, mostra pesquisa Quaest
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva estão em empate técnico no segundo turno, com vantagem numérica para o senador do PL, mostrou nesta quarta-feira a primeira pesquisa Quaest da segunda rodada da eleição presidencial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva estão em empate técnico no segundo turno, com vantagem numérica para o senador do PL, mostrou nesta quarta-feira a primeira pesquisa Quaest da segunda rodada da eleição presidencial. Flávio tem 46% das intenções de voto contra 44% de Lula. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. Os indecisos são 1%, enquanto os que disseram que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum candidato somam 9%. A pesquisa registrou também o índice de rejeição dos dois candidatos, que mostrou Flávio com 54% e Lula com 53%. Flávio Bolsonaro venceu o primeiro turno da eleição presidencial com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. Desde sua vitória no dia 4, o senador do PL garantiu o apoio de três presidenciáveis do primeiro turno - Augusto Cury (Avante), que ficou em terceiro lugar, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), quinto colocado, e Romeu Zema (Novo), sexto - e de vários partidos. Enquanto isso, várias cidades registraram manifestações de apoio a Lula, a maior delas até agora em São Paulo no último [USN:L6N45X070 TEXT:"domingo"]. Na resposta espontânea, quando os entrevistados respondem sem ver antes os nomes dos candidatos, 43% citaram Flávio Bolsonaro, 42% apontaram Lula, 8% declararam voto em branco, nulo ou que não vão votar e 7% se mostraram indecisos. A sondagem da Quaest apontou também transferência de votos. Entre os eleitores de Caiado e Renan Santos (Missão), Flávio lidera com folga, enquanto entre os eleitores de Cury, Lula tem uma pequena vantagem. Já entre eleitores ausentes e que votaram em branco ou nulo, o presidente tem vantagem sobre o senador. A pesquisa, realizada entre sábado e terça-feira, também mostrou que 48% desaprovam o governo Lula (eram 49% na sondagem anterior), enquanto 45% aprovam (eram 44%). Já sobre a avaliação do governo, ela era negativa para 40% (ante 42% na pesquisa anterior), positiva para 34% (eram 33%) e regular para 24% (eram 23%).

item.title: Gael Monfils apparently retires before planned
item.description: Part-tennis standout and part-showman Gael Monfils has apparently retired ahead of schedule.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Part-tennis standout and part-showman Gael Monfils has apparently retired ahead of schedule. The 40-year-old Frenchman did the farewell tour this spring and summer, but had received a wild-card entry to the ATP Masters event in Paris in early November. It was presumed he would play his final competitive match in his home country. But Monfils appeared on the list of retired players list maintained by the International Tennis Integrity Agency and listed as "inactive" as of Oct. 5. Since this body oversees anti-doping protocol in the sport and Monfils would not be subject to those rules, he is ineligible to compete in professional tournaments. On Wednesday, the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, an ATP 250 event in Lyon which begins on Oct. 19, announced that Monfils had pulled out of an exhibition match that included countrymen Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, Gilles Simon and Richard Gasquet due to personal reasons. Monfils has not confirmed his retirement, but, similar to Serena Williams' comeback path, he would have to be available for drug-testing for six months before returning to competition. Monfils made it clear after his second round loss to Learner Tien at the 2026 U.S. Open -- which now appears to be his final profession match --that he plans to enter the business world and announced that he had signed on with a Swiss company to work in wealth management. Monfils won 13 ATP Tour titles and reached a career-high world ranking of No. 6 in 2016. He reached Grand Slam semifinals at the French Open in 2008 and at the U.S. Open in 2016. But Monfils was perhaps more well-known for his artistry on the court. Even in his later years, he would run down balls that many younger players would not even attempt and display acrobatic moves on overheads and a deft touch at the net. Monfils is married to Ukrainian tennis standout Elina Svitolina and the couple has daughter, Skai, who turns 4 on Thursday. --Field Level Media

item.title: US states seek children's data protections in Character.AI bankruptcy
item.description: A group of 40 state attorneys general on Wednesday urged a US bankruptcy judge in Delaware to protect young users of Character.AI and keep their data safe during the AI companion company's bankruptcy.
item.dc:creator: Dietrich Knauth
item.content:encoded: A group of 40 state attorneys general on Wednesday urged a US bankruptcy judge in Delaware to protect young users of Character.AI and keep their data safe during the AI companion company's bankruptcy. Character.AI [USN:L6N45Z08O TEXT:"filed for bankruptcy"] late on Monday and is seeking to use its Chapter 11 case to resolve the states' investigations and lawsuits, license its technology to Disney (DIS.N) for $20 million, and seek a buyer willing to take on its chatbot business. Abigail Ryan, an attorney for the states, told US Bankruptcy Judge Brendan Shannon in Wilmington that the states are negotiating a settlement with Character.AI over allegations that its chatbots impersonated licensed medical professionals and exposed children to sexualized and abusive interactions. Even so, Ryan said, the states want to make sure that any buyer of Character.AI's assets will protect users' chat histories and improve safety features. "We're willing to work with the buyers to find safeguards, but we don't want to see what has transpired in the past start over with a new purchaser," Ryan said at the company's first hearing in US bankruptcy court. "This company has collected some of the most private thoughts children have ever shared, and now those conversations could be sold off to the highest bidder," New York Attorney General Letitia James, a Democrat, said in a Wednesday statement issued just before the court hearing. NO OFFER YET Character.AI's attorney, Erin Fay, said she heard those concerns "loud and clear," but said that no buyer has yet made an offer for the company's user data or its operating chatbot business. The company's platform allows users to interact with and create generative AI characters customized by user prompts and often modeled on fictional characters, celebrities, and historical figures. Its active users spend an average of two hours a day talking to the chatbots. Beyond the states' claims, Character.AI has been sued by families who allege that its chatbots gave harmful advice, contributed to the suicides of two children, and exposed children to sexualized and bullying interactions. Character.AI has [USN:L6N3Y8144 TEXT:"reached preliminary settlements"] with five of those families. The company also faces investigations by the US government and by authorities in the UK, Italy, Russia and Australia. Disney has agreed to pay $20 million to license the company's technology and intellectual property, as well as hiring most of Character.AI's staff, but is not interested in the type of data that the state AGs are worried about, Fay said. Disney's asset purchase must be approved by the bankruptcy court, and it is subject to higher offers. Fay described a grim mood within the company in recent months, saying that employees "were very excited about the product and the user base" but had "lost faith in the company's trajectory." The company attributed its bankruptcy to legal expenses and the high price for computing power and AI talent, saying it was losing between $8 million and $9 million a month before filing for Chapter 11 protection. Character.AI's management became concerned about its ability to survive employee attrition by late summer. In September, Disney stepped in to hire most of the company's employees and allow them to work on keeping Character.AI afloat during a bankruptcy sale process and technology transition, according to court filings.

item.title: US company announces progress toward resurrecting the extinct dodo
item.description: A US biotech company says it is making progress toward its goal of resurrecting the dodo, the famous flightless bird with a large hooked beak, and returning it to its native Indian Ocean island of Mauritius, where humans drove it to extinction in the 17th century.
item.dc:creator: Will Dunham
item.content:encoded: A US biotech company says it is making progress toward its goal of resurrecting the [USN:KCN0VX2OO TEXT:"dodo"], the famous flightless bird with a large hooked beak, and returning it to its native Indian Ocean island of Mauritius, where humans drove it to extinction in the 17th century. Dallas-based [USN:L1N42V0QY TEXT:"Colossal Biosciences"] said on Wednesday it has used a newly developed AI platform to identify genetic changes that may be responsible for the dodo's distinctive craniofacial traits as its scientists pursue gene-editing targets to bring back this lost species. Colossal is planning to perform gene-editing to bring dodo traits into the cells of its closest living relative, the Nicobar pigeon. Native to some Southeast Asian islands, the Nicobar pigeon is known for its shimmering green and copper feathers and, unlike the dodo, can fly. The company said it is in the final stages of its analysis of the dodo genome, now filled to 95%. It also said it has made an advance that should shorten the time needed to test whether a genetic edit produces the desired trait. The company did not announce a timeframe for hatching a dodo. Colossal says it is dedicated to "de-extinction" — resurrecting vanished species. Last year, it said it had genetically engineered [USN:L2N3QM0N8 TEXT:"the dire wolf"] by editing the genes of the gray wolf, the extinct Ice Age predator's closest living relative, to add dire wolf traits. Besides the dodo and dire wolf, Colossal has four other species on its de-extinction list: the [USN:L1N3WI1ER TEXT:"woolly mammoth"]; the thylacine, also called the Tasmanian tiger; the [USN:L1N41B1O8 TEXT:"bluebuck antelope"]; and the moa, a large flightless bird. "The dodo is the world's best-known symbol of extinction caused by people. It disappeared within decades of humans arriving on Mauritius, largely because of the introduction of invasive species like rats and other animals they brought. Bringing it back shows extinction doesn't have to be permanent," Ben Lamm, Colossal's CEO and co-founder, told Reuters. "The big hurdles ahead are proving which genetic changes really matter, making many of those edits in a bird and passing them to the next generation, and preparing a safe home for dodos on Mauritius," Lamm said. The dodo was a ground-nesting bird about 3 feet (1 metre) tall and weighing up to about 50 pounds (23 kg). Having never encountered humans, dodos exhibited no fear of the people who reached Mauritius in the 16th century. Pressured by invasive species and human hunting, the last living dodo was seen in 1662. It has remained alive in popular culture including in Lewis Carroll's book "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland." GENOMORPH PLATFORM Ancient DNA is always broken into small pieces, so no ancient genome is perfectly complete, including that of the dodo. The new AI platform Colossal built is called GenoMorph. "The challenge was scientists only have one complete dodo genome, making it difficult to distinguish the genetic differences that made the dodo unique from ordinary genetic variation. GenoMorph effectively acts as a 'treasure map' for the dodo genome, narrowing hundreds of thousands of possible genetic changes into the targets most likely to explain its iconic beak and facial structure," Lamm said. Beth Shapiro, Colossal's chief science officer, said GenoMorph finds likely gene-editing targets for species with very little surviving DNA. Normally scientists compare many genomes from one species to find the genes behind a trait, but this is not possible with the dodo, Shapiro said. "So instead, GenoMorph studies how skulls and beaks develop across more than 70 living bird species and learns which genetic switches control their shape. It gave us a shortlist of about 2,300 candidates linked to beak size and shape. These targets are now being validated in the lab," Shapiro said. Colossal said it has expanded its colony of Nicobar pigeons in Texas to 36 birds following successful breeding among established pairs. It said this should help in studying Nicobar pigeon development, reproduction and genetics. Lamm said the company is working with Mauritian scientists, conservation groups and the Mauritius government on what bringing the dodo back to its native land might look like. "Getting Mauritius ready for dodos also means removing invasive predators and restoring habitat, which helps the native species living there now," Lamm said. "No release sites will be chosen until the ecological work and community consultation are finalized, but it is Colossal's goal to put our dodos back into their natural habitats in Mauritius."

item.title: Trading Day: Tech melt
item.description: US stocks fell sharply on Wednesday, with the Nasdaq clocking its biggest fall in three months, on surprisingly strong inflation data and deepening worries over the costs involved in financing the AI buildout. The inflation figures put a Fed rate hike later this month back on the table, which lifted the dollar to a fresh 18-month high.

item.content:encoded:
US [USN:L6N4600KR TEXT:"stocks"] fell sharply on Wednesday, with the Nasdaq clocking its biggest fall in three months, on surprisingly strong [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"inflation"] data and deepening worries over the costs involved in financing the [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"AI"] buildout. The inflation figures put a Fed rate hike later this month back on the table, which lifted the [USN:L4N46001K TEXT:"dollar"] to a fresh 18-month high. Today's Key Reads [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"US inflation heats up in September; Fed rate hike this month back on table"] [USN:S0N40K04E TEXT:"IMF calls for US to cut deficits amid bond woes, urges China to shift away from exports"] [USN:L6N45Z13S TEXT:"Why governments might secretly wish for an AI stumble: Mike Dolan"] [USN:L4N45Z1M8 TEXT:"As Wall Street banks finance and adopt AI, risks mount on both fronts"] [USN:L6N46015N TEXT:"Bond trading weakens for US banks as interest rate volatility affects investors"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Asia in the red, China -1%. [USN:L6N4600FQ TEXT:"Europe"] +0.4%, [USN:L6N4600MA TEXT:"UK"] +0.7%. Americas in the red: Nasdaq -1.9%, S&P 500 -1.1%. SECTORS/SHARES: Eight sectors on the S&P 500 fall, three rise. Tech -2.6%, healthcare and consumer staples +2.4%. "SOX" chip index -4.2%, down for sixth day, longest losing streak in nearly two years. Coreweave -15.5%, Dell -11%, Oracle and Marvell -9%. UnitedHealth, Moderna, Bristol-Myers Squibb all up 4-5%. FX: [USN:L4N46001K TEXT:"Dollar"] up strongly again, new 18-month high. Mexican peso, South African rand among the biggest EM FX decliners, euro, sterling, Swedish crown the biggest G10 losers. BONDS: US AI-related corporate bonds fall sharply, many to new lows. Yields rise, spreads widen. Longer-dated US Treasury yields fall 3-4 bps, curve flattens. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L1N46000C TEXT:"Oil"] up, WTI +1%. Gold -1%, silver -6.5%.

Today's Talking Points: AI bond blues Investor sentiment towards AI financing — or more pointedly, circular financing — is souring. Rapidly. Coreweave's 9.75% bond issued in July and maturing in 2031 on Wednesday yielded 16% and slumped to a new low in price. Meta's "Beignet Investor" bond maturing in 2049 is also hovering around its lows, and both bonds are down around 20% from issue. Oracle's 4.9% bond maturing in 2033 registered a record low today. You get the picture. Borrowing costs and spreads are spiraling higher, which deepens investors' concerns, risking further selling and intensifying the negative feedback loop. What stops the rot? In the near term, strong earnings and positive outlooks from CEOs and CFOs in the coming weeks might help. But if selling pressure on AI-related bonds and stocks persists, are we ultimately looking at some sort of intervention? Raising the stakes Talking of which, it's not unreasonable to think that the US government will end up taking stakes in some of the country's biggest AI/tech companies, either due to national security concerns, safety issues, or because they are simply "too big to fail". Or all of the above. As the battle with China for global AI dominance intensifies, the importance to Washington of the key US players is only going to increase. In fact, the Trump administration is already flexing its muscles in the private sector, most notably via its stakes in the US Steel/Nippon Steel partnership and Intel. According to the Cato Institute, the US government has done 35 equity-stake deals since June 2025. Prior to that, US equity deals were unheard of in non-crisis times, notes Cato's Scott Lincicome. Of these 35 deals, 11 are in semiconductor companies, and 9 are in quantum computing firms. The focus and direction of travel seem pretty clear. China's clear direction If there were any lingering doubt about how policymakers in Beijing are trying to generate China's economic growth, the latest trade data should put them to rest. Surging exports widened China's trade surplus more than expected in September, putting the country on track for another $1 trillion annual surplus, and in record time too. The external sector is booming, while the domestic economy remains shackled by subdued demand and investment. AI was a central part of the trade figures, as global demand for semiconductors and green-tech products boosted exports, and its place in US-China fault lines is becoming increasingly stark, fueling record Chinese surpluses and widening US deficits (and by extension, global imbalances), and the tech and resources war between the two countries.
